history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE / IDENTITY UNCERTAIN: this row names the 'Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Khammam Fort'. Khammam Fort stands on Stambhadri hill (17.245012, 80.146736 per Wikipedia), and Khammam's name itself derives from the 'Narasimhadri' temple on that hillock (Kambam/Kambham Mettu). This is very likely the same shrine already documented as seq 1008 (id stambadri-lakshmi-narasimha-swamy-temple-khammam) — the Sri Stambadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple on Narasimha Swami Gutta, Khammam town, roughly 1 km from the fort pin — but the two map pins differ and sources disagree on whether the hill shrine and the fort precinct are one complex, so the duplicate is probable but not confirmed; MERGE DECISION NEEDED with seq 1008. Alternative: Wikipedia's Khammam Fort article separately mentions a 'Lakshmi Narasimha swami temple in Brahmin bazar' as one of the oldest temples in Telangana, older than the fort itself — that town shrine may be the intended referent instead. Attributes reported for the Stambhadri hill complex: Kakatiya-era attribution (Pratapa Rudra per a single Velpu source, unverified), 3-tier rajagopuram and 32-pillared mandapam. CSV town (Khammam), district (Khammam) and state (Telangana) are correct.

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (Khammam Fort)
town_description: Khammam is a major city in Telangana on the Munneru river, named after the Stambhadri (Kambham Mettu) hill whose Narasimhadri temple gave the town its name. The roughly 1000-year-old Khammam Fort crowns the hill, and its precinct holds old temples, a Khilla masjid and palace ruins.
